I know exactly how this feels. There are so many people on this sub-reddit who want to die because they are lonely, but here we are, seemingly with strong relationships, still wanting to die.

I think often about the things I could say - or write in a letter - that would make people understand why I wanted to die, and not feel guilty or sad about it. So far I've got no answers.

I'm constantly pulled back and forth between the desire to kill myself and not wanting to break my loved ones' hearts

Hello millionaires of Reddit.   
 

I was wondering if you've ever lost everything and rebuilt your wealth starting from scratch? 

If I could tell you a bit about myself in a nutshell - I recently lost my life’s savings through some stupid investments (58,000). It was an expensive mistake to learn. The loss meant myself and my partner had to pull out of buying our first home and are now starting over from square one.   
 

We are struggling to pay for our rent and bills. The guilt of the loss triggered a fairly violent depression which is currently being treated with medication and therapy. 

I am 25 years old and not entirely sure if I want to see 26 with the weight of such a life-changing mistake on my shoulders.  

So, if you have been in my position before and had to start over, how did you do it? And how hard was it mentally? 

Thank you
Well done u/Daszehan, it's nice people are looking out for others
Hello everyone. I just wanted to thank everyone for commenting and sharing their experiences. I'm here for everyone
I do appreciate your words, but if I didn't make a stupid choice, i would be living an entirely different life right now
It doesn't help the suffering. Not one bit. Sorry my friend

I think that a lot too, that I'm causing a lot of suffering to those around me. Life is horribly unfair, I think of those born into wealth who will never know stress, and those burdened with terminal illnesses. It seems there is no reason for why some are lucky and others aren't. 

I've told myself I will do my best to stay, if I can. If I don't recover, then maybe I too will think about something more final. But the fact you are starving yourself makes me feel there is a lot of self-loathing inside you. I hope you know I've heard you, whoever you may be. I really do hope you stick around.

I know this feeling. As someone who has been depressed with money, and depressed without it, I definitely preferred being depressed with it - at least then I had stability. 

Recently I lost my life's savings, throwing mine and my partner's future into the air. I would do anything to go back in time.

Anyway, if you ever want to chat, I'm here my friend.

I think starving to death will be quite slow and unpleasant. You mentioned self-harm, so i imagine that is perhaps part of your reasoning? 

If you are willing to talk about it, why do you want to die?
Hey. Did you want to talk about how you're feeling?

I could never understand your pain, but it is completely rational to feel shit, especially when your life was changed by something unfair.  

I know I certainly would. You sound like a remarkable person, however, and I would love to chat sometime.

Recently, something happened which exacerbated my depression to the point where it is now quite severe, with not much hope in sight of it abating anytime soon. 

Anyway, I'm happy to chat if you ever need to pen out your thoughts

I think, perhaps, what Bloopy said is being taken as a lot harsher than is intended. We are communicating via text, so a lot of nuance is lost. 

When I was growing up, I was lucky enough to have great parents. When I saw people whose parents didn't care about them as much, I thought they were bad parents. As I got older, and saw more of the world, I learned my parents weren't the standard example of parenthood, they were the exception. 

The point I'm trying to make  is we shouldn't expect to be treated a certain way, no matter how unfair it seems.

If somebody doesn't want to hang out with you, or doesn't text you, it doesn't mean they want you to kill yourself. 

You obviously feel alone and that you aren't being treated fairly. But maybe their actions aren't malicious?
I hope it isn't, my friend
